title: Grateful Dead Live at Rose Palace on 1969-03-22
lineage: SBD > MC > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Sharp soundboard recording captures a blazing 1969 Rose Palace show highlighted by an epic Dark Star and soaring performances from Jerry, Phil and the drums.
ai_review.review: The SBD capture is generally crisp with a well‑balanced mix—Jerry’s tone shines, Bob’s guitar cuts through, and the drums are described as razor‑sharp.  Musically the night is a high‑energy burst of late‑‘69 fire, anchored by one of the era’s most celebrated Dark Stars, tight St Stephen and an aggressive The Eleven (though the tape ends early).  The biggest drawback is the incomplete set, but listeners still rate it among the season’s best.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly high praise for both performance and mix; only minor deductions for vocal hotness and missing portions of the show.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, sharp mix with clear drums and soaring bass; vocals a touch hot and drums slightly recessed in places.  Some reviewers note that the tape is incomplete, but the recorded sections are well balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Fast‑paced, punchy set that feels loose yet zip‑filled; transitions are purposeful and the band stays tightly locked despite the brevity of the recording.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for perfect tone, every note on the money, and soaring lead throughout Dark Star and other jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as soaring and colorizing the jams; “Phil bombs” vibe noted in several reviews.
band_member_comments.Bob: Guitar noted as chiming, chopping and a tad louder than Garcia’s Les Paul; his slice‑and‑dice work praised during transitions.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brief keyboard arpeggio mentioned early in Dark Star; overall keyboards are present but not dominant.
band_member_comments.Drums: Aggressive, loud, clear, razor‑blade‑like drumming; both Bill and Mickey (drummer) described as fired up and imaginative.
